headline_marked: Army officer: [[Ziaul Ahsan linked to Ilias Ali disappearance]]
headline: Army officer: Ziaul Ahsan linked to Ilias Ali disappearance
summary: A serving army officer testified before the International Crimes Tribunal that he overheard a coded conversation implying the enforced disappearance of the BNP leader.
details: An army officer, Imrul Kayes, testified before the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan was involved in the disappearance of BNP leader Ilias Ali in 2012.
Kayes, who served as a runner to Ziaul while he was the director of Rab Intelligence, claimed he witnessed activities and overheard conversations surrounding the event.
The witness testified that he overheard Ziaul tell Major General (retd) Tarique Ahmed Siddique, "Sir, we golfed Ilias as per your instructions," implying the enforced disappearance of the leader.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam explained that "golf" was a coded term used by military personnel to mean putting someone into a hole, or enforced disappearance.
Kayes also stated that after Ilias Ali went missing from Banani on April 17, 2012, he found the Rab headquarters' CCTV footage and weapon register had been destroyed.
Ziaul Ahsan is the sole accused in a crimes against humanity case, accused of orchestrating the enforced disappearance and murder of 104 people between 2010 and 2013.
caption:
A serving army officer claims he overheard a coded message: "we golfed Ilias" to describe the enforced disappearance of a BNP leader.

An army officer, Imrul Kayes, testified before the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan was involved in the disappearance of BNP leader Ilias Ali in 2012.

Kayes, who served as a runner to Ziaul while he was the director of Rab Intelligence, claimed he witnessed activities and overheard conversations surrounding the event.

The witness testified that he overheard Ziaul tell Major General (retd) Tarique Ahmed Siddique, "Sir, we golfed Ilias as per your instructions," implying the enforced disappearance of the leader.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam explained that "golf" was a coded term used by military personnel to mean putting someone into a hole, or enforced disappearance.

Kayes also stated that after Ilias Ali went missing from Banani on April 17, 2012, he found the Rab headquarters' CCTV footage and weapon register had been destroyed.

Ziaul Ahsan is the sole accused in a crimes against humanity case, accused of orchestrating the enforced disappearance and murder of 104 people between 2010 and 2013.

headline_marked: Australia [[romp to 3-0 series whitewash]] over Bangladesh
headline: Australia romp to 3-0 series whitewash over Bangladesh
summary: The visitors secured a dominant seven-wicket victory in the final T20I in Chattogram, completing a clean sweep of the series.
details: Australia completed a 3-0 series whitewash over Bangladesh with a seven-wicket win in the third T20I in Chattogram on Sunday.
Chasing a modest target of 110 runs, the Australian side reached the total in just 13 overs, led by Captain Mitchell Marsh, who scored 60 off 28 balls.
Bangladesh struggled heavily in the first innings, posting a total of 109 for eight after electing to bat first.
Stand-in captain Tawhid Hridoy was the only significant contributor for the hosts, scoring an unbeaten 61 off 51 balls.
The Bangladesh batting lineup collapsed early, losing three top-order wickets within the first five overs, slumping to 11 for three.
For Australia, Spencer Johnson was the standout bowler, taking two wickets for six runs in his four overs, while Nathan Ellis and Adam Zampa also claimed two wickets each.
Nasum Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, and Rishad Hossain each took one wicket for the Tigers.
The visitors had previously won the first match by four wickets and the second by seven runs, all three matches played at the Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium.
caption:
A complete clean sweep. Australia thrashes Bangladesh 3-0 in the T20I series.

Australia completed a 3-0 series whitewash over Bangladesh with a seven-wicket win in the third T20I in Chattogram on Sunday.

Chasing a modest target of 110 runs, the Australian side reached the total in just 13 overs, led by Captain Mitchell Marsh, who scored 60 off 28 balls.

Bangladesh struggled heavily in the first innings, posting a total of 109 for eight after electing to bat first.

Stand-in captain Tawhid Hridoy was the only significant contributor for the hosts, scoring an unbeaten 61 off 51 balls.

The Bangladesh batting lineup collapsed early, losing three top-order wickets within the first five overs, slumping to 11 for three.

For Australia, Spencer Johnson was the standout bowler, taking two wickets for six runs in his four overs, while Nathan Ellis and Adam Zampa also claimed two wickets each.

Nasum Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, and Rishad Hossain each took one wicket for the Tigers.

The visitors had previously won the first match by four wickets and the second by seven runs, all three matches played at the Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium.
